messages:
Talia: hey everyone, day 1 here. on mac Ventura with an M2. trying to get a clean dev environment. installed brew, asdf, pyenv, rust, node, but hitting a few weird issues: python builds failing with openssl errors, node native modules failing to compile (node-gyp), and my dotfiles repo has some zsh hooks that seem to break GUI apps launched from Finder. any tips?
Ben: welcome! :wave: quick checklist: make sure Homebrew is the ARM install in /opt/homebrew, and that your shell rc loads brew and asdf BEFORE any system paths. also Rosetta may be needed for some npm native builds.
Chris: for python/openssl errors on M1/M2 the usual fix is to point pyenv/build to brewed openssl and readline. e.g.:
```bash
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--enable-shared" pyenv install 3.10.12
```
Ben: node-gyp often needs Xcode cli and python from asdf. also for some packages brew's node or Rosetta node is used. try forcing the asdf shim first, and if you have to build an Intel-only binary, run terminal under Rosetta 2.
Talia: my dotfiles set a lot of PATH tweaks and zsh plugins. GUI apps (like VSCode launched from Spotlight) don't get my ~/.zshrc, so extensions see different PATH. how do you handle that?
Chris: recommended flow: launch VSCode via the Remote - WSL/Remote - Containers or from terminal with `code .` so it inherits your shell. alternatively, add minimal PATH exports to ~/.profile or ~/.zprofile which are read by GUI logins. e.g.:
```bash
# ~/.zprofile
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
```
Ben: also keep interactive-only bits (like fzf init) in ~/.zshrc and the PATH/bootstrap in ~/.zprofile. GUI shells tend to read the latter.
Talia: ok that makes sense. one more: 1Password CLI sessions for local services (I use REDWOOD_API_KEY for local dev). I can sign in interactively but Docker containers or dev servers started by launchd don't see the session. what's the best practice?
Ben: we usually use direnv + op read in .envrc per-repo. that way the env is injected when you enter the folder. sample .envrc: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op read "op://Redwood/Dev/REDWOOD_API_KEY")`. make sure to `direnv allow`.
Chris: if you need services that start outside an interactive shell, you can write a small wrapper that fetches secrets into a temporary env file (with strict permissions) before launching the process. avoid committing any secret files.
Talia: any quick advice about dotfiles sync? I forked the company dotfiles and symlinked stuff; a few hooks are failing in zsh plugin manager.
Ben: sync strategy: keep a tiny bootstrap in your dotfiles that clones the rest and runs a setup script. avoid executing unreviewed hooks automatically. we have an internal repo `dotfiles/redwood` with an approved install script. run that and then add your personal bits on top.
OnboardingBot: Hi Talia! Welcome to Redwood. Check onboarding guide: https://intranet/redwood/onboarding/mac-apple-silicon for M1/M2 tips (openssl/pyenv, node-gyp, Rosetta notes) and the recommended .zprofile + .envrc examples.
Talia: thanks folks, super helpful. I'll follow the pyenv openssl flags and split my rc into zprofile/zshrc. can ping for pairing if I get stuck. :thumbsup:
Chris: happy to pair on the pyenv build if you want. most of us have a small script in ~/bin/py-build that wraps the env exports.
Ben: FYI our VSCode extension pack: ESLint, Prettier, GitLens, Redwood Snippets. also install 1Password and the CLI if you haven't.
Talia: adding those now. appreciate the warm welcome! :heart:
